title: Tri-region scaling horizon & cadence
summary: Sprint-oriented capacity horizon for NA / EU / APAC with utilization bands, buffer triggers, and a four-wave rollout cadence. Designed to support mixed hosted/dedicated demand with flexible surge lanes and a warmed-cache metric for throughput planning.
content:
Executive summary:
This working doc defines a 24-week horizon and sprint cadence for scaling GPU capacity across North America (NA), Europe (EU), and APAC. It prioritizes: predictable latency for Hosted API, dedicated pools for Reserved customers, and fast reaction windows for cross-region failover.

Key objectives:
- Maintain average sustained utilization between 60–75% across fleet while keeping 95th percentile latency SLOs intact.
- Provide a minimum cold->warmed GPU buffer of 15% (by vGPU equivalent) per region for high-variance workloads.
- Roll out capacity in four discrete waves (every 6 weeks) with a week-long stabilization window after each wave.

Assumptions used in forecasts:
- Average token demand growth: 6.5% week-over-week for Hosted API (observed last 8 weeks).
- Dedicated contract commitments: two major deals onboarding in Q2 expected to add 420 vGPU-equivalent peak tokens per second by week 10.
- Model mix shifts: heavier long-context models increase average sequence length by 1.8x -> effective tokens/GPU throughput drops ~25%.
- Typical packing ratio (vGPU-equivalent per physical GPU): 4.0 for mixed-precision workloads; burstable to 4.8 with tighter placement.
- A warmed-cache GPU (has KV cache primed) services ~1.6x more throughput for chat-heavy traffic versus cold starts.

Capacity forecast (vGPU-equivalent units) by region and wave (24-week horizon):
- Baseline week 0 (current warmed capacity): NA 960, EU 560, APAC 320.
- Wave 1 (weeks 1-6) target add: NA +240, EU +160, APAC +80 (focus: baseline runway + 12% buffer).
- Wave 2 (weeks 7-12) target add: NA +360, EU +240, APAC +160 (add dedicated pools for two enterprise customers).
- Wave 3 (weeks 13-18) target add: NA +480, EU +320, APAC +240 (regional performance zones + cross-region fallback lanes).
- Wave 4 (weeks 19-24) target add: NA +200 (spot replacement + warm-cache reserve), EU +120, APAC +80 (conservative finalization).

Projected end-of-horizon capacity (week 24):
- NA: 960 + 240 + 360 + 480 + 200 = 2240 vGPU-eq
- EU: 560 + 160 + 240 + 320 + 120 = 1400 vGPU-eq
- APAC: 320 + 80 + 160 + 240 + 80 = 880 vGPU-eq

Utilization scenarios and thresholds:
- Green (operational): 55–75% sustained utilization. Proceed with normal cadence.
- Yellow (watch): 76–85% sustained utilization or 2x week-over-week request variance. Pause optional non-critical onboarding; accelerate Wave windows by up to 2 weeks.
- Red (action): >85% sustained utilization or repeated 95th percentile latency degradation >20% over SLO. Trigger emergency surge (cross-region routing, pre-approved spot purchases, throttle non-critical customers).

Buffer and warm-cache policy:
- Maintain a warmed-vGPU buffer: target 15% of total regional vGPU-eq. This is warmed via continuous low-priority synthetic traffic and priority pre-warm for scheduled rollouts.
- Cold-warm transition SLA: 10–20s for typical KV-prime sequences; plan for worst-case cold penalty in latency budgets for first 2 tokens.
- Warm-cache reserve is counted separately from headroom used for organic traffic (i.e., buffer cannot be consumed for burst without explicit approval).

Rollout cadence and gating criteria (per wave):
- Week -1: Pre-rollout validation (scripts, canary models, infra smoke checks).
- Week 0-4: Wave deployment window. Provision incremental pool in 2 phases: phase A (50%) then phase B (remaining) spaced 48–72 hours apart.
- Week 5: Stabilization & observability ramp; evaluate cost metrics and perf regressions.
- Gating checks to pass before next wave: 95th p99 latency within budget, error rates <0.5% above baseline, warmed-buffer intact, and cost per token within forecast +/- 8%.

Sprint alignment to engineering calendar:
- Each rollout wave aligned to a 6-week product/infra sprint. Infra teams: provisioning, bake images, network policies. Runtime teams: kernel selection & quant profiles. Product: traffic migration and canary traffic sets. SRE: runbooks and rollback procedures.

Surge lanes and failover rules:
- Pre-authorized surge pool in NA that can be re-routed to EU/APAC for 72-hour emergencies (capacity peering via inter-region routing). Surge capacity limited to 18% of NA pool to avoid overcommit.
- Cross-region cost threshold: if cross-region traffic causes >12% uplift in egress costs month-over-month, re-evaluate surge policy.

Cost / efficiency notes:
- Expect unit token cost delta when shifting to newer GPU families; factor a 7–12% efficiency improvement when successful kernel/quant profiles are applied. Use Optimize recommendations to re-balance pack ratios after Wave 2.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: delayed supply (HW delivery slips by 4+ weeks). Mitigation: accelerate spot procure, increase warm-cache ratio, tighten batching to regain 8–12% effective throughput.
- Risk: model mix shifts greater than expected. Mitigation: staged canaries with long-context models and rolling quant profiles; reserve a small pool for low-latency models.
- Risk: control-plane bugs during scale. Mitigation: limit concurrent provisioning to one major region per week and require playbook signoff.

Operational runbook highlights (short):
- Pre-rollout checklist: capacity test harness, canary prompt set, KV-priming shim, monitoring dashboards ready, rollback image snapshot.
- Incident play: identify whether latency spike is cold-cache vs. packing saturation using KV hit metrics and scheduler queue lengths.
- Emergency steps: enable cross-region fallback -> throttle non-critical routes -> spin spot-backed pools -> apply kernel fallback (less aggressive quant).

Next steps / action items:
- Infra: produce a per-zone procurement calendar with vendor ETA and onboarding queue (due 2026-03-10).
- Runtime: publish expected throughput degradation matrix for long-context models (due 2026-03-08).
- Product/Ops: finalize canary prompt sets and contract onboarding timelines (due 2026-03-12).

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally sprint-oriented and prescriptive; please call out any constraints from vendor SLAs or procurement that would break the wave cadence.
- Open questions: exact vGPU-equivalent mapping for the new A100->H100 conversions (we may need to re-baseline after procurement).

Appendix (quick tables):
- Quick check: if Wave 2 is delayed by 3 weeks, NA utilization projects +9% at week 12 -> move Wave 3 earlier or enable surge lane by default.
- Warm-cache priming cadence: daily low-priority job that cycles 20% of buffer each 8 hours to maintain KV evictions alignment.

--END OF WORKING DRAFT--
